**Claim:** PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`domain:ui` execution seat) — branch `claude/issue-6388-simpleform-submithandler-order`. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` in the same label write.

## Pre-dispatch gate

**1. Thread read.** Triage comment (19:53:35Z) read in full. It is **ruling-inherited and queue-ready with no open question**: #6300's triage direction — *"when a `submitHandler` is declared, a missing `dataSource` must never bypass it"* — already answers this cell, and PR #6386 implements it for the five variant renderers. Same family, same defect class (#6176's), no semantic difference claimed for `simple`.

**2. Serial constraint — DISCHARGED.** Triage wrote *"same file family as the in-flight MasterDetailForm work (#6372/#6371) and PR #6386 — clear or serialize at claim time."* Re-measured: **PR #6386 merged 19:40Z**, **PR #6393 (#6372+#6371) merged 19:56Z**. Both on `main`. Nothing is in flight in `packages/plugin-form/` — the one live dev (#4929) is in `plugin-grid` / `plugin-kanban`. Clear, not serialized.

**3. Premise.** The carve-out in `SimpleObjectForm.handleSubmit` (`packages/plugin-form/src/ObjectForm.tsx`) is checked **before** the persistence chain, so a declared `submitHandler` is never reached. Measured by the filer at `onSuccess` 1 / `submitHandler` 0. ⛔ **Re-derive it on the merged tree** — `main` has moved several times since it was filed.

## Scope — the resolution triage named

**Move the inline-fields carve-out *after* the `submitHandler` check, matching the five.** That is the whole change.

⭐ **The shape to copy is now on `main`**, landed by PR #6386 (#6300): the five variants gate on `!dataSource && !schema.submitHandler && hasInlineFieldSource(schema)` and refuse from *inside* the persistence chain, after the `submitHandler` branch. `packages/plugin-form/src/submitTarget.ts` holds the shared rule. **Read it and reuse it** — ⛔ do not write a sixth private copy of the predicate.

⚠️ `SimpleObjectForm` uses `hasInlineFields`, the five use `hasInlineFieldSource`. **Measure whether they mean the same thing** before assuming you can swap one for the other. If they differ, say how and which is right for `simple` — ⛔ do not silently widen or narrow `simple`'s carve-out while "aligning" it.

**Pin lands beside the family's**, in `packages/plugin-form/src/submitTargetRefusal.test.tsx` **block 1**, as triage specified.

## Tests

- ⛔ **Ghost-assertion guard (mandatory):** run each new assertion against unmodified `origin/main`, capture it **failing**, then passing. Both readings in the PR body.
- ⛔ **Degenerate-control guard:** keep a case with **no** `submitHandler` declared, where the inline carve-out still fires and `onSuccess` is still the write. That is `simple`'s legitimate behaviour and it must survive. Name which fixture is the control.
- Cover the inverse too: `submitHandler` declared **and** a `dataSource` present — `submitHandler` still wins, per #6176.
- ⛔ Do not weaken or delete any assertion in `submitTargetRefusal.test.tsx`; PR #6386 just established that file.

## Boundaries

⛔ Scope is `packages/plugin-form/src/ObjectForm.tsx` and its pin. Do not revisit the five variants — they are correct as of #6386. Do not touch `packages/spec`. Do not widen any accept set: this is declared-≠-enforced restoration, restoring a documented seam (`submitHandler` *"hands the collected values to the host INSTEAD of calling dataSource.create / dataSource.update"*).

## Ground rules

Worktree-first: `git worktree add ../objectui-6388 -b claude/issue-6388-simpleform-submithandler-order main && cd ../objectui-6388 && pnpm install`. ⛔ Never `git stash` — `refs/stash` lives in the common `.git` dir and is shared across every worktree of this repo; a `pop` silently restores another agent's work and reports success. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`. Changeset: `patch`, `@object-ui/plugin-form`. Run the repo's fast checks before pushing. Open the PR as **draft** with `Fixes #6388` and report back — the PM lands it, ⛔ never self-merge.

Size: S. Model: opus (this seat's default tier).

## ⭐ The predicate warning paid off — and "aligning" them would have been a bug

My dispatch order said: *"`SimpleObjectForm` uses `hasInlineFields`, the five use `hasInlineFieldSource`. **Measure whether they mean the same thing** before assuming you can swap one for the other."* The dev measured, and they do not.

**Verified against `origin/main`:**
```
packages/plugin-form/src/ObjectForm.tsx:483
  const hasInlineFields = schema.customFields && schema.customFields.length > 0;

packages/plugin-form/src/submitTarget.ts:135
  return sectionsAreFullyInline(s?.sections);        ← limb (b), which the above has no equivalent of
```

They agree on limb (a) and diverge on limb (b). And the dev found *why it matters*: `SimpleObjectForm` **does not read section fields as a field source** — its sections path builds a name-keyed map and filters fields already resolved from `customFields` or the object schema, merging only `visibleOn` / `span` / `colSpan`. An all-inline-sections form with no adapter therefore resolves **zero fields**.

⇒ Swapping the predicate would have widened `simple`'s carve-out into **a success signal for a form that collected nothing** — precisely #6300's defect class, reintroduced one card after fixing it.

⭐ **The tidy-looking move was the wrong one.** Two predicates with near-identical names, one used by five renderers and one by the sixth, is exactly the shape that invites a drive-by unification — and the reason it is wrong lives in a *different function* than either predicate. `simple` keeps its own; only the refusal (`noSubmitTargetError()`) is shared, and **block 3's new boundary case pins that decision mechanically** rather than leaving it as a comment someone will later "clean up".

The dev also found the pre-chain `DataSource is required` throw sat ahead of the carve-out too, so the seam was unreachable in **both** target-less shapes — not just the one the card named.

## Instrument discipline

Ghost guard: fix committed first, then **only** `ObjectForm.tsx` reverted to `faa863dce`, mutation confirmed **by blob hash** (`b1098755` → `379c0a53`, equal to base, different from HEAD), restored under a trap and verified by an empty `git diff HEAD` plus the hash back at `b1098755`. Against the unmodified implementation: **2 failed / 33 passed**, and the two failures are exactly the two new pins — including the filer's `onSuccess` 1 / `submitHandler` 0 reproduced. After: 35 passed.

⭐ **Degenerate control named, and its passing on both legs is deliberate**: block 3's *"CONTROL — no seam declared, the carve-out still fires"* asserts `onSuccess` is still the write **and still receives the raw collected values**. The #6176 inverse (seam declared *with* a `dataSource`) also passes on both legs, deliberately — *"the ordering defect was reachable only through the `!dataSource` carve-out."* Stating why a control passes on both sides is what makes it a control rather than a filler test.

`submitTargetRefusal.test.tsx`: `git diff --numstat` 142 insertions, **0 deletions** — nothing weakened, as required.

## ⛔ A gap in MY process the dev caught

> a sibling dev seat IS active in `packages/plugin-form/` (worktree `objectui-6394`) — it appeared in the shared verify-lock queue **after** the pre-dispatch gate declared the package clear.

The dev is right, and the cause is mine: I ran #6388's shadow check, saw `plugin-form` clear, and then **dispatched #6394 into the same package in the same batch**. My shadow check looked at what was *in flight* — not at what I was *about to dispatch alongside it*.

⭐ **Same-batch collisions are invisible to a per-card shadow check.** That is a fourth distinct failure mode this round, and it is not covered by "census the shape, not the symbol." The fix is procedural: when dispatching a batch, run the shadow check **against the batch as well as against the in-flight set**.

Harmless this time — #6388 is `ObjectForm.tsx`, #6394 is `MasterDetailForm.tsx`, disjoint — but I am **sequencing the two merges** rather than assuming independence, as the dev asked.

⭐ Also correct: leaving PR #6406's duplicated session-URL footer alone (the platform appended one at creation) rather than "repairing" it with an edit. Cosmetic churn on a PR body is not a fix.

⛔ **Not enqueued** — CI had not converged at report time. `in_progress` is not a verdict.
